fixes.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) Moses is told to go up and see it, and the LORD says plainly that He has given it to the Israelites.

Nope, no one is mentioned waiting up there. The LORD says, "Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites." (Numbers 27:12) The elders aren't in this verse, so they can't be the answer.

Ooh, I know why this one sounds right. A leader goes all that way with his people, so you'd expect him to walk in with them. But God doesn't say that. He says, "After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Moses sees the land, and God says he will be gathered to his people.
Aaron it is. God says Moses will be gathered to his people "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The word "brother" is right there, and so is the name.
Korah is a fair guess, but it's not the name God gives here. He says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) The verse names Aaron, and it calls him Moses' brother.
Caleb is a good name to know, but it's not the one in this verse. God says, "…as your brother Aaron was…" (Numbers 27:13) Look for the word "brother" and you land on Aaron.
That's it. After hearing that he'll be gathered to his people, Moses asks the LORD to "…appoint a man over the congregation" (Numbers 27:16) I think that's a request for the people, not for himself.

Yes, sheep. Moses asks for a leader so that the congregation of the LORD "will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) Jesus uses a picture like that too when He sees the crowds. They were "harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd." (Matthew 9:36)

Soldiers is a fair guess, but Moses picks a different picture. He says the congregation of the LORD "will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) I think a shepherd is a much gentler picture than a commander.

Travelers is a good guess, I'll give you that. But Moses uses a different picture. He says, "…so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd." (Numbers 27:17) It's sheep, friend.
Spirit is right. God calls Joshua "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) That's the description God gives right here.
Strength is a natural guess, but it's not the word God uses. He says, "…a man with the Spirit in him…" (Numbers 27:18) The thing God points to is the Spirit.
A staff handoff would make a great picture, wouldn't it? But the text doesn't say that here. God's instruction is, "…lay your hands on him." (Numbers 27:18) No staff in this instruction.

Right, False. God wants it out in the open. Joshua is to "…stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation…" and be commissioned "…in their sight." (Numbers 27:19) That's the opposite of private.

That's the reason God gives. He says, "Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him." (Numbers 27:20) The authority is given so that the congregation will obey.
Counsel, you got it. God says Eleazar "…will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim." (Numbers 27:21) Eleazar does the seeking, and he does it for Joshua before the LORD.

True. The text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it shows him doing it: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation. I think that's worth noticing.

This one is True. After God finishes speaking, the text says, "Moses did as the LORD had commanded him." (Numbers 27:22) Then it shows him doing it: he took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation.
